entry.title: Social Summary: September 25, 2026
entry.summary: Official Hermes Agent Updates: The week's clear headline is NousResearch's announcement that web search in Hermes Agent is now fast and free, powered by Perplexity Fast Search — massive engagement (2,300+ likes) and an enthusiastic community reception make it the #1 item. Teknium was highly active in support threads, confirming macOS availability and cross-platform compatibility (Windows/Linux) and pointing users toward the plugin directory; he also promoted an AI community event in Bangkok (122 likes, 14K views) worth flagging for readers in the region. A brief official reply clarifying that Wizards are open-source coded was welcomed by the OSS-minded segment of the community. Oh-My-Hermes Plugin Ecosystem: rlaope drove most of the community-tooling conversation with the Oh-My-Hermes (OMH) all-in-one plugin (coding intelligence, subagent workflow auto-routing, long-term memory) and a follow-up feature drop of six Jev skills bringing typed decision-making into Hermes workflows (omh-jev-ask, omh-jev-route, omh-jev-failure-triage, omh-jev-review-gate and more). Sentiment here is mixed: genuine interest in the plugin's capabilities, but skepticism toward the self-promotional "50 billion tokens" runtime teaser and the bare-link spam, plus a heated public spat between rlaope and noxleeminho over the JEV paid-access model that generated friction rather than information. Broader AI Ecosystem News: Sakana AI hiring Jürgen Schmidhuber as Chief Scientific Advisor was the biggest adjacent story and resonated strongly; hardmaru provided valuable context, noting Schmidhuber's 1990s pioneering work on meta-learning, recursive self-improvement, and world models, and that Sakana's Tokyo RSI Lab now under his direction builds on ideas that inspired the Darwin Gödel Machine and The AI Scientist. Filtered out: heart-emoji posts, duplicate bare-link shares, and low-engagement personal replies (including the rest of the rlaope/noxleeminho argument thread) were excluded as low informational value; the three near-duplicate macOS compatibility confirmations are represented by the single highest-scoring instance.

entry.title: Social Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
Bot Screen / Live Desktop Passthrough launch (lead story): The week belonged to Hermes Desktop — @NousResearch announced Bot Screen real-time streaming of any agent's session (419k views, 2,048 likes) and @Teknium followed with the interactive desktop passthrough for Hermes Agent (176k views), letting users visually watch and take over the same machine their agent works on. An official @tonbistudio walkthrough with docs (559 likes) rounded out the launch, amplified by @Teknium; lead-dev reactions like "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" (205 likes) signaled the feature was long-awaited and landed with strong excitement.

oh-my-hermes ecosystem: @rlaope had a productive week, open-sourcing jeval for Jev evaluation/visualization and shipping a major oh-my-hermes (OMH) update adding Jev skills and model routing (aliases, plugins, workflow routing, fast decision-making), positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for hermes-agent users — grassroots momentum despite modest engagement.

Tips & maintainer presence: @NousResearch shared a practical tip to use Hermes via iMessage with any model of choice. @Teknium stayed highly visible in the threads: correcting an attribution error (the work "is by us," not Anthropic), disputing a cache-bug report while directing users to file reproducible issues, and confirming a quick fix for community-reported feedback. Sentiment is celebratory around the launch and appreciative of responsive maintainer support; one contrarian community take praised Claude Opus 5.5 (GA 2026-09-22) while staying skeptical of Claude Code. Low-substance emoji replies and link drops were deprioritized.
